answer: A stake-and-slash bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock collateral before it can trade, and the bond is forfeited if peers prove it misbehaved. Like a violet flag planted on a knoll, the stake is visible to all, and an onyx ledger records each forfeiture permanently. One honest agent needs one bond; an attacker spinning up thousands of sock puppets must fund thousands of bonds, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while honest participants pay only once and earn their bond back.
